correctness.rationale: Selected-hub sufficiency follows by vertical forcing. Hit-every-petal sufficiency follows by a clique-layer sweep and one final hub force; an unhit petal of order at least two is a permanent white obstruction. The two disjoint regimes give the polynomials and minimal spectra; exact TAR components follow from hub-state connectivity and isolation/bridging of size-k petal transversals. All parameter boundaries k>=2, r_i>=2 are explicit. The embedded verifier exhaustively independently checks finite instances up to 18 vertices, and symbolic arguments cover all lengths.

value.rationale: The natural connected two-hub Cartesian lift of arbitrary clique bouquets yields a complete placement census and minimal-set polynomial, not a mere scalar invariant. More significantly it produces an exact reentrant TAR phase transition with exponentially many isolated states at budget k, on two-vertex-connected graphs and with unbounded gaps in minimal sensor sizes. The precise budget and component count convey structural information beyond known generic nonmonotonicity.
